simple.meaning: חֲלָק (chălâq) is a Hebrew word meaning “a part.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: חֲלָק (H2508) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Ezra 4:16, with occurrences in Ezra, Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חֲלָק (H2508) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in חֲלָק (H2508) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: חֲלָק (chălâq) / H2508 is traced through Ezra 4:16, Daniel 4:12, Daniel 4:20 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: We inform the king that, if this city is built and the walls finished, then you will have no possession beyond the River.

timeline.evidenceText: We inform the king that, if this city is built and the walls finished, then you will have no possession beyond the River.

The leaves of it were beautiful, and it had much fruit, and in it was food for all. The animals of the field had shade under it, and the birds of the sky lived in its branches, and all flesh was fed from it.
The tree that you saw, which grew, and was strong, whose height reached to the sky, and its sight to all the earth;

definitions.full: H2508. chalaq חֲלָק noun [masculine] portion, possession, lot (see Biblical Hebrew); — absolute ׳ח possession in land Ezra 4:16 ; suffix חֲלְקֵהּ Dan 4:12 , 20 , i.e. his appointed lot.
